questions.prompt: Why is `expect("config.toml must exist")` preferred over `unwrap()` when panicking is intentional?

options.text: It includes a descriptive context message in the panic output

options.text: Binds `user` in the enclosing scope on match, or executes the diverging `else` block (must `return`/`break`/`panic!`)

questions.prompt: Why are Rust iterators like `.map()` and `.filter()` called lazy?

options.text: They do no work until consumed by an adaptor/terminal like `.collect()`, `.sum()`, or a `for` loop

questions.prompt: What does a lifetime annotation `'a` in `fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str` express?

options.text: That the returned reference will remain valid at least as long as the shorter of `x` and `y`'s borrows

questions.prompt: What does `T: 'static` as a trait bound (e.g., `std::thread::spawn`) mean?

options.text: `T` contains no non-`'static` borrowed references (owned types like `String` and `i32` satisfy `T: 'static`)

questions.prompt: What does `move | | println!("{name}")` do in a closure?

options.text: Forces the closure to take ownership of captured variables instead of borrowing them
Prevents calling the closure more than once

questions.prompt: Which closure trait is implemented by a closure that consumes (moves out of) a captured value?
What does `map.entry(key).or_insert(0)` on a `HashMap` avoid?

options.text: Performing two separate hash lookups (one to check existence, another to insert)

questions.prompt: Why should function parameters usually accept `&str` instead of `&String` and `&[T]` instead of `&Vec<T>`?

options.text: Deref coercion lets `&str` / `&[T]` accept both owned (`&String`/`&Vec<T>`) AND slices/literals without extra allocations

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `#[cfg(test)]` on a `mod tests` block?

options.text: Excludes the test module from normal `cargo build` binaries and compiles it only during `cargo test`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Rust's module and visibility system. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `pub` makes an item visible to parent/external modules
`pub(crate)` restricts visibility to the current crate only
Submodules cannot access private items of their parent module
Items inside a module are private by default

questions.prompt: What does `Drop::drop(&mut self)` do when a value goes out of scope?

options.text: Runs deterministic cleanup (closing files, releasing locks, freeing buffers) automatically before memory is reclaimed

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `impl Trait` in argument position (`fn f(x: impl Read)`) vs `dyn Trait` (`fn f(x: &dyn Read)`)?

options.text: `impl Trait` uses static dispatch (monomorphized per concrete type); `&dyn Trait` uses dynamic dispatch via a vtable (supports heterogeneous collections)

questions.prompt: What does `#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]` require on a `struct`?

options.text: All fields must implement `PartialEq` (and `Eq` for reflexive equality—note `f64` implements `PartialEq` but NOT `Eq` due to `NaN`)

questions.prompt: What does `Result::ok()` do?

options.text: Converts `Result<T, E>` into `Option<T>`, discarding any `Err` value

questions.prompt: What does `vec.windows(2)` return on a slice `&[10, 20, 30]`?

options.text: An iterator of overlapping 2-element slices: `&[10, 20]` and `&[20, 30]`

questions.prompt: Match each `Option` / `Result` combinator to its behavior.

questions.prompt: Why should you prefer `.unwrap_or_else(|| expensive())` over `.unwrap_or(expensive())`?

options.text: `.unwrap_or(...)` eagerly evaluates `expensive()` even when the value is `Some`/`Ok`; `.unwrap_or_else` evaluates lazily

questions.prompt: What does `From<A> for B` automatically give you in Rust?

options.text: The reciprocal `Into<B> for A` implementation via the standard library blanket impl

questions.prompt: What is a turbofish `::<>` (e.g., `"42".parse::<i32>()`) used for?

options.text: Explicitly specifying generic type parameters when type inference needs a hint

questions.prompt: What does `super::helper()` refer to inside a submodule?

questions.prompt: What does `collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()` do when iterating over `Result<T, E>` items?

questions.prompt: What does `#[derive(Default)]` require on a struct?

options.text: Every field's type must implement the `Default` trait

questions.prompt: What is a trait object `&dyn Summary` composed of in memory?

options.text: A fat pointer (two pointers): one to the data instance and one to the type's vtable

questions.prompt: Why can't a trait with `fn clone(&self) -> Self` be used as `dyn Clone` (not object-safe / dyn-compatible)?

options.text: Returning `Self` by value has an unknown size at compile time behind `dyn` erasure

questions.prompt: What does `BufReader::new(file)` improve over reading 1 byte at a time from `std::fs::File`?

options.text: Batches reads into an in-memory buffer, drastically reducing OS syscall overhead

questions.prompt: What does `Option::as_ref()` do on `opt: &Option<String>`?

options.text: Converts `&Option<String>` into `Option<&String>` so you can inspect the inner value without moving out of `opt`

questions.prompt: What is lifetime elision in Rust?

questions.prompt: What is a `build.rs` file in a Cargo package?

questions.prompt: Why does Rust forbid returning a reference to a local variable from a function?

options.text: The local variable is dropped when the function returns, so the reference would dangle
